source: RiverNexa decision framework, Team Recycllux, 14 Nov 2026 (From measurements to decisions)
disclaimer: Not an operating procedure. Thresholds are indicative and must be calibrated per site with local managers. A reading informs a decision; it does not trigger pumping, releases, fish transfers, navigation restrictions or changes to nuclear operations.

parameters.name: Water depth
parameters.question: How much water remains, and where?
parameters.measure: Calibrated depth sensor or a surveyed water-level reference at fixed points. Local depth is not river stage.

thresholds.text: Flag when the depth or water-level target agreed for this habitat and season is approached; leave a buffer for inspection. There is no universal wetland minimum in cm.
A repeated fall beyond the site's agreed rate of change, or mapped loss of inundation around priority habitat, requests a targeted field check at fixed points.

thresholds.alert: Below a habitat or intake operating limit
thresholds.text: Escalate when a validated reading breaches the manager's ecological target or the operator's documented intake or pump limit.
Compare official fairway soundings with draught and clearance. A wetland reading cannot certify a navigable route.

parameters.name: Dissolved oxygen
parameters.question: Is there enough oxygen for aquatic life?
parameters.measure: mg/L with temperature (and % saturation), at dawn and at representative depths; calibrated, cleaned sensors.

thresholds.text: EPA: generally stressful for fish. Confirm the reading, check the trend and prepare the local response.
EPA: generally too low to support fish. Treat a credible breach as urgent and notify the responsible manager.
Hypoxia: rapid assessment and response matter more than the label.

thresholds.alert: Rapid overnight decline / repeated dawn lows
thresholds.text: Escalate a falling trend likely to breach the site's target before dawn, even if the latest reading is above 5 mg/L.

parameters.name: Salinity
parameters.question: Is the water becoming too salty for its use?
parameters.measure: Raw conductivity (dS/m or µS/cm) and temperature, with the conversion method; confirm changes with water samples.

thresholds.alert: Crossing 0.5 ppt at a normally fresh site
thresholds.text: USGS freshwater class boundary, not a toxicity limit: prompts an intrusion check.

thresholds.alert: Sustained rise above the seasonal baseline
thresholds.text: Investigate a change beyond the site's agreed normal range, including rate and duration.
Slight to moderate restriction: review crop sensitivity, soil and drainage.
Severe restriction: seek agronomic review before continued use.

parameters.name: Water temperature
parameters.question: Is heat making a difficult situation worse?
parameters.measure: Daily peaks and dawn conditions, together with oxygen, at representative locations and depths.

thresholds.text: A species reference range, not an alarm band.
Check sustained exposure, dawn oxygen and fish behaviour; prepare the agreed heat response.

thresholds.alert: High temperature plus oxygen below target
thresholds.text: Prioritise heat combined with DO below 5 mg/L, a steep oxygen decline or visible distress.

thresholds.alert: Cooling water near a plant limit
thresholds.text: Use the plant's own intake measurements and approved limits. No generic reactor trigger is proposed.

fish: Confirm depth at fixed points, check oxygen and inlets; top up with suitable water if permitted; consider partial harvest or transfer only with fish-welfare checks.
Revise stocking, storage and drought contingency plans; assess deeper refuges or pond repairs.
irrigation: Check intake usability and allocation; combine with soil moisture and crop stage; reschedule permitted irrigation; switch source only after quality checks.
Adapt crop mix, scheduling and storage to reliable supply.
wetland: Inspect mapped drying hotspots and refuge connections; assess gates or request an authorised transfer; protect sensitive areas from disturbance.
Restore hydrological connections and agree seasonal targets and water-allocation plans.
authority: Verify gauges, storage, downstream needs and travel time; review abstraction limits and feasible environmental releases under the drought plan.
Revise drought allocation rules and reservoir operations, accounting for energy and flood-control trade-offs.
nuclear: Use official intake levels and hydrological forecasts to assess margins; prepare output changes only under approved procedures. A wetland alert is context, not a control signal.
Evaluate cooling-water resilience through licensed engineering review.
port: Consult official fairway depths and berth soundings; adjust loading, timing or transport mode.
Use verified low-water histories for fleet, berth and logistics planning.

fish: Confirm the zone; start or increase safe aeration; reduce or stop feeding and fertilising; consider screened water exchange or partial harvest.
Match stocking and feed to oxygen capacity; invest in aeration, backup power and alarms.
irrigation: Do not stop irrigation just because the source has low oxygen; if runoff is implicated, coordinate source inspection.
Improve nutrient budgeting, runoff and drainage management.
wetland: Check refuge pools and report fish distress; inspect blooms or pollution with agencies; aerate only small managed refuges.
Restore connectivity and reduce nutrient pressures with catchment partners.
authority: Sample upstream, downstream and outlet water; assess feasible flow or outlet changes; verify release quality first.
Review release structures, operating rules and catchment nutrient measures.
nuclear: Notify the plant's environmental team if its receiving water is affected; verify intake and outfall permit requirements.
Improve environmental monitoring and mitigation within the permit where evidence supports it.
port: Share berth observations and follow pollution or navigation instructions.
Include water-quality evidence in environmental planning for recurrent events.

fish: Check pond and intake salinity against the stocked species' tolerance; pause an intake that exceeds the farm's limit; avoid abrupt changes.
Review intake protection, storage, species suitability and source redundancy.
irrigation: At ECw 0.7-3.0 dS/m review the crop and soil; above 3.0 seek advice; switch or blend tested sources where allowed.
Track soil salinity and drainage; choose suitable crops and sources.
wetland: Map affected inlets and sample connected pools; assess gates or a freshwater top-up only if connectivity and permits allow.
Restore freshwater connections and agree a seasonal salinity envelope.
authority: Combine salinity profiles with flow, levels and coastal conditions; review feasible releases or abstraction changes.
Include salt intrusion in drought scenarios and allocation rules.
nuclear: If a change reaches the plant supply, specialists compare verified intake chemistry with operating specifications.
Assess treatment and materials through licensed engineering review if repeated.
port: Salinity alone does not imply inadequate draught; notify berth or environmental teams of confirmed changes.
Assess local water-quality and infrastructure implications with specialists.

fish: Check oxygen first; intensify aeration and adjust feeding; avoid handling in the hottest period; exchange with cooler water only if suitable.
Plan stock density, aeration and pond refuges around summer conditions.
irrigation: Use the alert as a prompt to check weather, soil moisture and crop stage; schedule from those data, not water temperature alone.
Adapt calendars, crop choices and irrigation design to heat risk.
wetland: Inspect priority pools and confirm cooler refuges also have enough oxygen; limit disturbance.
Restore connections and vegetation or shade consistent with habitat objectives.
authority: Check outlet temperature and oxygen as well as volume; avoid thermal shock or cold, oxygen-poor releases.
Review outlet design and environmental release rules.
nuclear: Compare actual intake temperature, river conditions and discharge limits; plan output changes only under existing procedures.
Assess cooling resilience through licensed engineering and environmental review.
port: Review official low-water forecasts if hot weather coincides with falling levels.
Include verified heat and low-water episodes in seasonal planning.
